idea.Name: geometry_lifted_trispace_som
idea.Title: Geometry-Lifted TriSpace SOM for Self-Calibrating Full-Wave Inverse Scattering
idea.Short Hypothesis: For an unknown antenna pose, the receiver-side Green-operator derivative admits a canonical minimum-norm lift into a retained SOM current space plus an orthogonal irreducible data residual; coupling this lift to the full-wave state equation yields a second state-consistency witness, and their joint rank characterizes local pose hiding and can support a reduced self-calibration algorithm.
idea.Related Work: Equivalent currents and contrast sources, classical SOM and twofold SOM, source/receiver-extension full-waveform inversion, inverse scattering with transmitter localization, CSI calibration, blind calibration, SAR/radar autofocus, pseudoinverse lifts, variable projection, and subspace perturbation are established antecedents. The retrieval-bounded candidate contribution is only their type-correct full-wave/SOM synthesis: restrict the geometry-to-current lift to a declared retained current space, retain the orthogonal unrepresentable residual, separate receiver pseudo-current from transmitter-induced physical current, and couple the result to a state-equation consistency witness. Never claim first or globally novel.
idea.Abstract: We investigate self-calibrating full-wave inverse scattering when an antenna array pose changes the Green operators used by subspace optimization methods. At the independent-current level, we separate receiver-side re-sampling from the physical induced-current change caused by illumination. Given a retained SOM basis, we define the minimum-norm pose-equivalent current by a restricted pseudoinverse and prove an orthogonal decomposition into representable and irreducible data components. Reparameterizing the joint data and state linearization produces a state-consistency witness and an exact finite-dimensional condition for a pose direction to be hidden by retained current and real contrast variations. We test the identities, the vacuity of unrestricted full-row-rank equivalence, spectral-coordinate drift and rank events, receiver-versus-transmitter semantics, state-based disambiguation, and a reduced nonlinear calibration prototype in a deterministic 2D Helmholtz solver. Claims remain local, finite-dimensional, model-conditional, and retrieval-bounded.

datasets: Deterministic synthetic 2D scalar Helmholtz contrast-source scenes on a world-fixed grid using the corrected self-cell quadrature and analytic Green derivatives from the existing project harness.

Small single- and multi-pose Tx/Rx arrays with separately controlled receiver-only, transmitter-only, and co-moving SE(2) perturbations; include full-row-rank, deliberately rank-deficient, limited-aperture, and SVD-truncated cases.
Low-dimensional real contrast bases and several deterministic pose initializations/noise seeds for the nonlinear self-calibration comparison.
baselines: Unrestricted full-current pseudoinverse versus retained-rank SOM lifts.
Analytic receiver sampling, physical current, and total pose derivatives versus centered finite differences.
Wrong-pose fixed SOM, direct joint full-wave contrast-pose least squares, and geometry-lifted reduced data-plus-state calibration.
Hard SVD truncation versus a declared soft spectral filter near threshold crossings.
Data-only pose cancellation versus joint data-and-state consistency.
metrics: Lift reconstruction and orthogonality residuals, irreducible residual norm, lift norm, singular values, cutoff, ranks, and condition numbers.
SOM projector distance/leakage, subspace-bound ratio, spectral gap, threshold-crossing diagnostics, and soft-filter continuity.
Centered finite-difference errors for H_S, delta-j physical, and total B; null-current energy discarded by data-only projection.
Norms and ranks of R_U, D_U, T_U, and stacked pose signature; constructed hidden directions and gauge/anchor controls.
Map error, pose error, data residual, state residual, effective variables, runtime, convergence rate/basin, noise sensitivity, and retained failures.
Experiments.compute_estimate: Apple Silicon CPU only. Reuse the existing dense small-grid solver and cached factorizations. Begin at N=6 or N=8 for nonlinear optimization, then perform one modest refinement diagnostic if stable. No CUDA, GPU infrastructure, neural training, daemon, database, or web UI.
steps: Read the complete run instructions and theory seed; independently check the signs and spaces in the proposed propositions.
Implement E1 and retain the full-row-rank counterexample showing why unrestricted equivalence is vacuous.
Implement E2 using projector comparisons rather than raw singular vectors; expose a rank event deliberately.
Implement E3 with separate receiver, transmitter, and co-moving finite-difference checks.
Implement E4 and verify the exact finite-dimensional hiding condition after realification; include one confounded and one disambiguated case.
Implement E5 as an actual deterministic reconstruction comparison over several initializations or preserve a reproducible failure diagnosis.
Synthesize only executed results and write the paper draft with an originality firewall and explicit limitations.

Risk Factors and Limitations: A full-row-rank unrestricted sensing operator makes every data perturbation current-equivalent; failing to retain this negative control would make the central claim vacuous.
The canonical lift depends on whitening, realification, current norm, retained basis, and regularization; it is not metric-free.
Small singular values make the equivalent current unstable, and hard rank thresholds create discontinuous coordinate changes.
Receiver re-sampling produces a pseudo-current, whereas transmitter motion produces a physical induced-current change; combining them before the state equation can double count pose effects.
On a world-fixed homogeneous grid G_D is pose independent; a moving G_D belongs to a different model.
The exact TSOM domain fold is not verified in the project sources, so Phase-I experiments may use only a truncated SOM basis.
Finite-dimensional local rank does not prove global convergence, continuum stability, or hardware self-calibration.
The literature screen is retrieval-bounded and source/receiver-extension FWI is a close conceptual antecedent.
A nonlinear benefit may be initialization-dependent or absent; negative results must remain visible.

report.summary: Executed all five planned experiments (E1-E5) in a deterministic 2D scalar Helmholtz inverse-scattering harness. The finite-dimensional core claims are supported: the retained-rank SOM lift is non-vacuous and satisfies the orthogonal data decomposition, the joint data/state rank condition exactly characterizes local pose hiding, and the geometry-lifted reduced parameterization is lossless for identifiable pose while freezing hidden directions. Honest negative findings remain visible: unrestricted full-row-rank equivalence is vacuous, point-transmitter theta is structurally gauged, and the state-consistency witness T_U did not discriminate good from bad pose estimates in the tested setting.
key_results: E1: G_s is full row rank (8/8; singular values 1.67e-3 to 2.19e-3). Unrestricted full-rank lift reproduces receiver re-sampling to machine precision (||R_full||/||b|| = 5.5e-16), confirming vacuity without rank restriction. Retained-rank r=4 lift leaves irreducible residual ||R_U||/||b|| = 0.784 and verifies Q^H R_U orthogonality to 8.9e-18. Self-cell diagonal matches i*h^2/4 to 5.1e-4.

E2/E2b: 1D rx sweep shows avoided crossing only: min sigma4-sigma5 gap = 1.23e-6 at rx=0.42; hard projector jump 1.426 vs soft-filter jump 0.134 (~10.6x). 2D (rx, ry) scan finds true degeneracy sigma4=sigma5 at (0.16135, 0.16135) with gap 1.4e-15; hard projector jump 1.424 vs soft-filter 0.127.

E3: Analytic receiver, transmitter, and co-moving pose derivatives match centered finite differences at O(eps^2). rx errors 2.2e-3 to 2.2e-9 and theta errors 1.5e-4 to 1.3e-10 over eps=1e-2 to 1e-5. Transmitter check cross-validates the physical-current chain at J-level and data-level.

E4: With H = [retained current G_sV_r, real-contrast data G_sJ_chiPhi] realified: confounded regime (r=6, K=3) has rank(H)=15 of 16 data dimensions, giving an exact 2-dim hidden subspace (min singular values ~4.5e-16 receiver-only, ~4.3e-16 co-moving). Disambiguated regime (r=2, K=1) has rank(H)=5, no hiding (receiver/comoving min singular values 0.642/0.446). Constructed hidden direction has data-only residual 5.3e-16 against col([Q,W]) vs real-contrast-only residual 0.947; state witness T_U=0.733. Visible direction gives 0.131 vs 0.935 (T_U=0.674).

E4 gauge/anchor: a scalar point transmitter has only a 2D pose manifold; the theta derivative is exactly collinear with tx/ty for all phi0, so transmitter-only B_t always has rank 2. This is structural, not removable by an anchor angle.

E5: Wrong-pose fixed contrast-only inversion fails (residual 0.296, map error 0.199). Direct joint GN and geometry-lifted reduced GN at r=4 give identical solutions, recovering pose to 3.4e-3 and map to 2.3e-2 with residual 0.020 below the 0.032 noise floor. At r=6 the reduced parameterization drops to n_vis=1 visible pose DOF; recovered pose error 0.044 is almost entirely hidden (visible component 0.0015), residual 0.034, map error 0.024-0.040. Far hidden offset is unrecoverable by construction (bad init stalls at residual 0.16).
E5 state witness: T_U is consistently high (0.81-0.89 across estimators), quantifying the pseudo-current nature of the lift, but it did not discriminate good from bad pose estimates in this setup.

run_e2_e4.py - E2 spectral drift/rank event and E4 hiding-condition experiment driver.
run_e2b_gauge.py - exact 2D degeneracy search and point-transmitter gauge diagnosis.

results_e1_e3.json, results_e2_e4.json, results_e2b_gauge.json, results_e5_final.json - saved numerical results.
plot_*.png - generated figures for finite-difference errors, rank events, hiding diagnostics, and E5 recovery.
completed_steps: Read/checked idea and built a self-contained 2D scalar Helmholtz harness with analytic Green derivatives.
E1: implemented lift/decomposition and retained the full-row-rank negative control showing unrestricted equivalence is vacuous.
E2/E2b: implemented projector-comparison spectral sweep, exposed an exact 2D degeneracy, and compared hard vs soft filtering.
E3: implemented and finite-difference-checked separate receiver, transmitter, and co-moving pose derivatives.
E4: implemented and verified the finite-dimensional hiding condition with confounded, disambiguated, hidden, visible, and gauge cases.
E5: implemented and ran nonlinear self-calibration comparison, converged with direct joint GN and geometry-lifted reduced GN, and reproduced hidden-direction failure behavior.
Synthesized executed results and documented limitations, negative findings, and future directions.
dead_ends: Initial E5 GN with fixed lambda=1e-6 and backtracking was under-converged; replaced by adaptive LM, then by a mathematically clean reduced parameterization.
Earlier projected-Jacobian reduced variant stalled in the r=6 regime; identified as a solver-path artifact and superseded by run_e5_final.py.
One E5 initialization ('pert_neg') accidentally equaled the zero init due to spec arithmetic, leaving only 2 distinct starts in the 3-init medians.
Transmitter theta gauge could not be removed by phi0 anchoring because it is structural for a scalar point source; reported as a finding rather than fixed.
The state-consistency witness T_U did not discriminate good from bad pose estimates in the tested setting.
next_steps: Use a multi-transmitter or oriented array so theta is genuinely identifiable for transmitter-only or co-moving self-calibration.
Add a state-consistent reduced variant with the retained-current auxiliary c as an explicit variable penalized by T_U so the state witness participates algorithmically.
Run more noise seeds and SNR levels, including retained failure diagnostics rather than only medians.
Consider a soft spectral filter instead of hard rank truncation throughout the nonlinear loop.
Scale to larger N and multiple scenes, and re-check threshold/rank events under larger deterministic grids.

unresolved_issues: The state-consistency witness T_U did not discriminate good from bad pose estimates in the tested setting, so the proposed state-based disambiguation mechanism is unvalidated. The paper must either develop and test a variant that does discriminate, or explicitly demote/remove that claim and clarify what role T_U plays.

All experiments are in a single deterministic 2D scalar Helmholtz setting with low-dimensional real contrast bases. A full-paper claim needs at least one additional feasible setting, such as a different frequency, discretization/grid size, contrast complexity, or limited-aperture geometry, to show the rank/lift behavior is not an artifact of one configuration.

There is no adequate replication across multiple noise realizations or random initializations for the central reconstruction claims. Robustness to noise near the reported 0.032 floor and convergence-basin behavior need multiple seeds and quantitative summaries.

Ablation of key components is too sparse: only r=4 and r=6 are reported for the reduced reconstruction, with no systematic sweep over retained rank r, regularization/whitening choices, or soft-filter parameters.

The transition from identifiable receiver pose (r=4) to mostly hidden pose (r=6) is only shown at two points. The paper should characterize the rank transition, hidden/visible DOF decomposition, and noise threshold more comprehensively.

The structural gauge finding for point-transmitter theta is an important negative result, but its implications for algorithm design and model misspecification are not developed; an extended/transmit-array case is needed to show whether the method is useful beyond receiver-only pose.
verdict.reasoning: The executed study is substantive and contains valuable sanity checks: the unrestricted full-row-rank vacuity is honestly demonstrated, the retained-rank lift satisfies the orthogonal decomposition, analytic derivatives are verified against finite differences, an exact rank event is exposed with soft-filter mitigation, and the finite-dimensional pose-hiding condition is supported by controlled confounded/disambiguated cases. The reduced and direct joint reconstructions are also compared, with hidden directions correctly frozen. These are strong components for a theory-plus-synthetic paper. However, the empirical breadth is still below a full-length top-venue bar: it is a single deterministic 2D Helmholtz scenario with no systematic noise replication, few rank/regularization ablations, and only isolated reconstruction examples. Most importantly, the proposed state-consistency witness T_U failed to discriminate good from bad pose estimates, leaving a central aspect of the method unsupported. The core idea remains worth keeping, but the study should be deepened and the failed witness either fixed or removed before writing a full paper.
